topics.name: Cloud fundamentals
topics.description: Core Google Cloud services and how to choose between them.

practices.name: Core services
practices.description: A practice with one single-answer question and one multi-answer question.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud service runs a container image without requiring you to manage a cluster?
questions.explanation: Cloud Run is a managed container platform. You give it a container image and it handles scaling and the underlying infrastructure.
alternativeExplanations: Compute Engine gives you virtual machines, so you manage the operating system and runtime yourself.
Correct. Cloud Run runs containers on fully managed infrastructure and scales with requests.
Google Kubernetes Engine runs containers, but you still manage a cluster and its node pools.
Cloud Functions runs event-driven functions, not arbitrary long-running container images.

questions.prompt: Which of these are managed services that run code without requiring you to manage a cluster?
questions.explanation: Cloud Run and Cloud Functions are managed compute services. You do not provision or maintain a cluster for either one.
alternativeExplanations: Correct. Cloud Run runs containers on managed infrastructure.
Compute Engine gives you virtual machines, so you manage the operating system and runtime yourself.
Correct. Cloud Functions runs event-driven functions on managed infrastructure.
Cloud SQL is a managed relational database, not a compute service for running your code.

topics.name: Networking basics
topics.description: IP addressing, DNS, and transport-layer behaviour.

questions.prompt: Which transport protocol provides reliable, ordered delivery of a byte stream?
questions.explanation: TCP establishes a connection, acknowledges segments, and retransmits lost data to preserve order and reliability.
alternativeExplanations: UDP is connectionless and does not guarantee delivery or ordering.
Correct. TCP provides a reliable, ordered byte stream.
ICMP carries control and error messages, such as ping requests.
ARP resolves IPv4 addresses to link-layer addresses; it does not carry a byte stream.
